Issue Reading note
Fuel surcharge moves headline revenue and margin in opposite directions Surcharge revenue was C$1,483m in FY2025 and enters the income statement at a 100% incremental operating ratio. FY2025 headline revenue grew 3.7% and 5.4% excluding it; H1 2026 grew 5.0% headline and 2.4% excluding it. Any growth or margin figure quoted without the split is not comparable across the two periods.
The KCS control date of 2023-04-14 breaks every series KCS was held in a voting trust and equity-accounted from 2021-12-14 to 2023-04-13, then consolidated. FY2023 holds about 8.5 months of KCS; FY2024 is the first clean full year and FY2025 the first clean growth rate.
KCS purchase accounting is a permanent wedge between GAAP and core adjusted 290bp of FY2025 operating ratio, of which 250bp is amortization of fair-value adjustments that runs over the acquired assets' useful lives. GAAP operating ratio 62.8%, core adjusted 59.9%.
No commodity line has a margin CPKC reports one segment. The nine lines are a revenue disaggregation with no allocated cost, so every line-level margin below is an explicit estimate with its range.

Three further facts bear on the whole document. Every CPKC and CN figure is Canadian dollars; UNP, NSC, CSX and BNSF report in U.S. dollars, and the two are never placed in one column without the rate. Mexico produced 18% of FY2025 revenue and holds C$11,326m of long-lived assets, and CPKC does not publish a profit, margin or return for it. Executive compensation, board pay and insider ownership are in the management information circular furnished as an 8-K exhibit and in a Part III amendment to the 10-K; CPKC has filed no DEF 14A since 2017.

1. Business description, model and unit economics

CPKC moves loaded freight cars from origin to destination over about 20,000 route miles across Canada, the United States and Mexico, and it owns and operates the only freight railway spanning all three (10-K FY2025, Item 1).▪ Revenue is priced per shipment, invoiced when the bill of lading is processed and recognised over the transit. FY2025 revenue of C$15,078m is 4,514.0 thousand carloads at C$3,273 each, plus C$302m of non-freight income from leasing, interline switching, passenger contracts and subsurface and fibre-optic rights. The same identity holds on the ton-mile basis: 219,420m revenue ton-miles at 6.73 cents.

CPKC reports one operating segment. The nine commodity lines below are a revenue disaggregation under ASC 606 with no allocated operating cost.▪

Source: 10-K FY2025 Note 4 and Item 7, Lines of Business. FY2023 holds about 8.5 months of KCS, so the FY2024 growth column is not organic. Geography (Note 28): Canada C$7,243m, United States C$5,124m, Mexico C$2,711m. Sub-splits the filing renders only as pie-chart images appear in the September 2026 investor deck: Canadian and U.S. grain are half the grain line each, Canadian grain is 68% regulated, coal is 61% Canadian, and international intermodal is 65% Vancouver and 13% Lázaro Cárdenas [deck: investor presentation September 2026, slides 23–32].

Who pays: No single customer exceeded 10% of total revenues in 2023, 2024 or 2025 (10-K FY2025, Note 28), which on 4.5m carloads is a granular book. Three lines run through narrow channels anyway: all export potash is marketed by Canpotex, the Nutrien and Mosaic joint venture, or by K+S Potash Canada; almost all Canadian metallurgical coal originates at Elk Valley Resources mines in southeast British Columbia; and 46% of intermodal revenue is international containers whose routing ocean-carrier alliances set annually. Those three counterparties set volume on C$2,897m of FY2025 revenue.▪

Bulk shippers — grain, coal, potash, fertilizers, 36% of freight revenue — buy unit-train capacity to a fixed port, and the alternative at a Saskatchewan potash mine or an Elk Valley pit is CN. Merchandise and intermodal shippers choose between rail, truck, pipeline and barge on landed cost and transit time. Creel's description of the competitive test against CN's new Mexico access: "we're a single-line move. They're a multiline move… it's still a 3-line move" (Morgan Stanley Laguna conference, 2026-09-17).

Unit economics

The unit CPKC prices is the carload; the unit that consumes cost is the gross ton-mile. Because no operating expense is allocated to any line, the cost column below is constructed from published car tare and lading weights, scaled so that the nine estimated gross-ton-mile figures reconcile to the disclosed system total of 403,891m. A bottom-up build on a low-tare set gives 383,593m and on a high-tare set 459,285m, so the disclosed total falls inside the method's own range and each line's cost figure inherits that spread.

Carloads and revenue per carload are as filed (10-K FY2025, Lines of Business). Estimated gross ton-miles and every figure derived from them are [estimate: car tare and lading physics scaled to the disclosed system GTM total of 403,891m; the underlying bottom-up build spans 383,593m to 459,285m, and each line's cost figure inherits that spread]. The point estimate allocates 100% of operating expense by gross ton-mile; the parenthetical range is the result when 20% and 40% of expense is instead allocated by carload, which is the sensitivity that matters for terminal-intensive traffic. Allocated costs sum to C$9,469m by construction, and freight contribution of C$5,307m plus C$302m of non-freight equals reported operating income of C$5,609m.

Potash coming out negative is where the method breaks, and the break is informative. A Canpotex unit train is a dedicated closed loop from Saskatchewan to Vancouver with no intermediate switching and the heaviest train weights on the network — CPKC attributes its 3% FY2025 increase in average train weight to "moving longer and heavier Grain and Potash trains" (10-K FY2025, Performance Indicators). A single-factor allocation penalises the lines that are cheapest per ton. The five merchandise lines survive every allocation rule tested at 47–59% contribution and account for 48.8% of freight revenue; the bulk and intermodal lines, 51.2% of revenue, fall in a band from roughly zero to 44% that the disclosure cannot narrow. Narrowing it requires train-miles and switch events by line, which CPKC does not publish.

The yield table is substantially a weight table. Revenue per ton-mile spans 7.2x across the nine lines, from potash at 3.32 cents to automotive at 23.85. Converted to revenue per gross ton-mile the same nine span 2.6x, from potash at 2.16 to metals and minerals at 5.73.▪ Automotive moves from 3.5x the system average per ton-mile to 1.24x per gross ton-mile, because a tri-level autorack weighs roughly 45 tons empty and holds roughly 18 tons of vehicles and CPKC shuttles the empty rack back to the assembly plant. Most of automotive's headline yield premium pays for hauling the rack; a premium remains, at C$5,483 per carload against a C$3,273 system average.

Grain, the crude leg of energy and chemicals, and the land bridge need more than a row.

Grain is weather. Canadian production of all principal field crops reached 107.0 Mt in 2025, the largest on record, 10.4% above 2024 and 16.2% above the 2020–2024 average of 92.1 Mt; the prior record was 100.1 Mt in 2020, and western Canada alone came in 23% above its five-year average (agriculture.canada.ca, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Grain supplied 52% of the C$913m of freight revenue growth from FY2024 to the twelve months ended June 2026, and 74% of the H1 2026 increase. Canadian-origin grain is half the line, so a Canadian crop reverting to its five-year mean removes about 7% of the whole grain line, roughly C$225m of revenue and C$70–100m of operating income at the constructed 31–44% contribution margin [estimate: 14% tonnage reversion applied to the Canadian half of the grain line per the September 2026 deck's 50/50 split, at FY2025 grain yield and the §1 contribution range]. Creel describes the dependence the same way: "in Canadian Pacific, we're a grain railroad… we're also still benefiting from being that one-trick pony" (Morgan Stanley Laguna, 2026-09-17).

The crude leg of energy and chemicals has not grown. DRUbit heavy crude moves single-line from Hardisty, Alberta to Port Arthur, Texas, and the 10-K describes it as "cost competitive with pipeline transportation" (10-K FY2025, Energy, Chemicals and Plastics), which means it clears when pipeline space is tight. Trans Mountain reached full utilisation of its 890,000 bbl/d capacity in June 2026 (hydrocarbonprocessing.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web], and Canadian crude-by-rail exports were 1.8% of total Canadian crude exports in 2025, a 13-year low (cer-rec.gc.ca, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Creel on what the merger did not deliver: "Crude oil, that was a big piece for us… That hasn't came" (Morgan Stanley Laguna, 2026-09-17). The base survived; Q2 2026 energy and chemicals RTMs rose 6% partly on higher DRU and conventional crude volumes.

Management's growth story and the earnings driver are different lines. Management's story is near-shoring and the three-country land bridge, sized by Brooks at about C$100m of revenue in 2023, over C$600m in 2026 and a stated path to C$1bn, of which 65% moves between western Canada and Mexico (Q2 2026 earnings call, 2026-07-29). At C$600m that is 4.0% of FY2025 revenue and it grew about C$140m in 2025.▪ Over the same window grain supplied C$470m of the C$913m of FY2024-to-LTM freight growth. The land bridge grows faster than the company; the crop moves more dollars.

Pricing

There is no backlog and no contracted volume. "Each bill of lading or service request is a distinct performance obligation… The short duration over which freight rail services are delivered generally means that there is an immaterial value of outstanding performance obligations" (10-K FY2025, Note 2). Master service agreements fix a price framework; the volume is re-won carload by carload. Four mechanisms set price, and management controls one of them.▪

Mechanism Coverage FY2025 / current level
Negotiated freight rates The commercial book Guided 3–4% at the 2023 Investor Day; management describes renewals at 3.5–4.5% in 2026
Maximum revenue entitlement Western Canadian export grain to Vancouver and Thunder Bay, about 7% of total revenue 2026-27 volume-related composite price index +0.646%, against +3.11% for 2025-26 and +12.7% for 2022-23
Fuel cost adjustment Indexed to On-Highway Diesel in Canada and the U.S. and PEMEX TAR Irapuato in Mexico C$1,483m, 10.0% of freight revenue
FX translation The U.S. and Mexican books Each C$0.01 in CAD/USD moves annual revenue about C$78m and operating expense about C$45m

The regulated share is now bounded. Grain is 22% of freight revenue, Canadian grain is half of that, and 68% of Canadian grain is entitlement-regulated, which gives roughly 7% of freight revenue, about C$1.1bn▪ [estimate: September 2026 deck slides 23 and 24 applied to FY2025 freight revenue; the three inputs are whole percentages]. The Canadian Transportation Agency's own crop-year determination corroborates the level and shows CPKC at the cap: for crop year 2024-25 CPKC's regulated grain revenue of C$1,066,938,687 exceeded its entitlement of C$1,064,278,437 by C$2,660,250, and CPKC paid the overage plus a 5% penalty of C$133,012 to the Western Grains Research Foundation; CN came in C$5,913,453 below its own entitlement (canada.ca, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. C$1,067m is 33% of the FY2025 grain line and 7.1% of total revenue, on a crop year that does not align with the fiscal year.

Realized price meets the guide on one disclosed measure and misses it on the other. Stripping fuel surcharge and the disclosed FX effect from freight revenue:

The 3.7-point gap in H1 2026 is length of haul, which Brooks puts at "up year-over-year about 3%" (Q2 2026 call). The per-carload measure ignores that incremental miles consume gross ton-miles and fuel; the per-ton-mile measure ignores that incremental miles are sold at positive contribution on an already-scheduled train. At 4.5m carloads, each percentage point of length-of-haul extension adds roughly 2,200m RTMs and, at the FY2025 marginal ex-fuel cost of 1.43 cents per RTM against a 5.99-cent core yield, roughly C$130m of revenue at about a 76% contribution.

Decomposing the C$553m freight revenue increase: volume +C$536m, commodity mix −C$26m, rate +C$44m. Ninety-seven percent of the increase was volume, and the mix drag visible in cents per ton-mile comes from longer and lower-rated lanes inside each commodity line; the between-line mix effect was −C$26m.

Depreciation at 21.3% of expense does not vary with volume, and C$373m of it is amortization of KCS fair-value adjustments. Labour is priced by four-year Teamsters Canada Rail Conference agreements at 3% a year from 2024 through 2027, settled by binding arbitration on 2025-05-30. Removing fuel surcharge from revenue and fuel expense from cost isolates the non-pass-through business: FY2025 organic operating expense rose C$186m on 7,962m additional ton-miles, 2.34 cents per incremental RTM against a 4.32-cent average, and 1.43 cents against 3.53 excluding fuel from both sides. Roughly 40–55% of an average cost dollar recurs on the next ton-mile, which is why volume growth and volume decline both reach operating income with unusual force.▪

FY2025's 68% lands inside the 60–70% Velani guided at the 2023 Investor Day. H1 2026 at 40% does not.▪ Velani attributed 120 basis points of Q2 2026 operating-ratio headwind to higher casualty costs and stock-based compensation, worth roughly C$50m; adding that back restores the quarter to about 69%. Unit cost is where the productivity shows: ex-fuel operating expense per ton-mile was 3.527 cents in FY2025 against 3.578 in FY2024, a 1.4% decline while contracted wages rose 3%, and it was flat in H1 2026. Average employees were 19,967 in FY2025 against 20,144, which CPKC attributes to completing KCS systems integration in 2025.

Growth requires almost no working capital. Accounts receivable were C$2,029m at 2025-12-31, 49 days of revenue, against accounts payable and accrued liabilities of C$2,751m; the cash conversion cycle is negative 61 days. Capital intensity is the offsetting demand: FY2025 additions to properties were C$3,102m, 20.6% of revenue and 1.54x depreciation, of which approximately C$1,500m renewed depleted rail, ties, ballast, signals and bridges, C$236m went to network improvements and growth within the track-and-roadway line, and C$923m bought Tier 4 locomotives against C$335m of locomotive spend in FY2024.

2. Key technologies and technical differentiators

What separates CPKC from CN, UNP, NSC, CSX and BNSF is a route structure, a Mexican concession and a statutory pricing regime. None of those is a technology.▪ CPKC does not disclose a technology or information-systems capital line; "Other" additions of C$340m in FY2025 is the maximum, and that category also holds intermodal equipment, work equipment and vehicles [estimate: FY2025 10-K Capital Programs table; information systems is one of four asset types inside the C$340m, so 11% of capital spending is a ceiling and the true figure is well below it]. Over the same year CPKC spent C$923m on locomotives and C$1,736m on track and roadway.

Precision Scheduled Railroading is an operating discipline: run trains to a fixed schedule, move cars on published plans, and size locomotive, car and crew fleets to that plan (10-K FY2025, Item 1, Strategy). Every North American Class I adopted a version between 2017 and 2021, and CPKC's FY2025 core adjusted operating ratio of 59.9% (GAAP 62.8%) compares with UNP's GAAP 59.8% and CN's GAAP 61.9%. Fuel efficiency is directly comparable — both CPKC and CN publish U.S. gallons per 1,000 gross ton-miles — and CPKC burned 18% more fuel per gross ton-mile than CN in FY2025 and 19% more in Q2 2026.▪ Locomotive productivity of 166 gross ton-miles per operating horsepower against UNP's 139 is not comparable: CPKC's denominator excludes units offline, tied up or in storage, and 292 locomotives were in storage at 2025-12-31. CPKC last published a level for average train weight and average train length in the FY2021 10-K (9,967 tons, 8,200 feet) and has reported only percentage changes since, while CN and UNP publish levels.

The 8,500-foot High Efficiency Product grain train is the clearest case of technology producing a commercial result. The train grows from 7,000 to 8,500 feet, new hopper cars three feet shorter hold 10–20% more grain each, and an 8,500-foot consist holds 147 cars instead of 112, raising loaded tonnage from 10,500 to 15,000 tonnes, an increase of 44% (2018 Investor Day, Joan Hardy).▪ The 10-K rounds this to "approximately 40% more grain". The hard part is not the train: to qualify for the HEP rate a customer's origin elevator and destination terminal must each load or unload an 8,500-foot train within 16 hours, clear of the mainline, in a single string. Customers spent about C$600m matching that specification, Richardson International committed C$70m across nine sites, and CPKC went from 6 HEP-capable facilities in 2018 to a stated target of 66 by mid-2024 (2023 Investor Day, John Brooks). Once an elevator is rebuilt to CPKC's loop-track geometry the switching cost to another railway is the cost of the elevator.▪ The limit shows in tonnage: CPKC moved 30.66 million tonnes of Canadian grain in the 2025-26 crop year, an all-time record that exceeded the 2020-21 record by about 72,500 tonnes, 0.2% (prnewswire.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Five crop years of customer investment and a C$500m hopper fleet produced almost the same peak tonnage as the fleet that preceded them. The harvest sets the ceiling; the HEP return appears in fewer train starts, fewer crews and redeployable capacity.

DRUbit and the Diluent Recovery Unit solve a physical problem: Alberta heavy crude is roughly 70% bitumen and 30% diluent by volume, and the diluent exists only to make the blend flow through a pipeline. Stripping it at origin produces a product that is non-hazardous for transport and lets a train hold about 30% more crude.▪ The barrier is not the chemistry. It is exclusive rail access at Hardisty, a single-line haul to the U.S. Gulf Coast, and a ConocoPhillips 10-year take-or-pay contract for 50,000 bbl/d that justified a third party's plant (usdg.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Phase 1 reached its run rate in 2021 and no further 50,000 bbl/d increment has been sanctioned.

Tier 4 locomotives are a purchase decision. Wabtec and Progress Rail sell the same units to every Class I; CPKC's order book is 170 Wabtec units and 65 Progress Rail units, about 10% of a 2,307-unit fleet whose average age is 24 years. What they bought shows in one series:

U.S. gal / 1,000 GTM FY2019 FY2020 FY2021 FY2022 FY2023 FY2024 FY2025 H1'26 Q2'26
CPKC 0.955 0.942 0.931 0.955 1.026 1.033 1.034 1.017 0.992

Consolidating KCS moved the metric 7% worse in one year and it stayed there for three. Q2 2026 is the first material improvement since 2021, 4% better year on year and the first sub-1.00 quarter since Q1 2023, which the 10-Q attributes to higher locomotive productivity. It does not close the peer gap: CN was at 0.836 in the same quarter and improved 3%.

Detection and inspection is where management's "at the forefront of technology" claim concentrates. Cold wheel technology is the real advantage: wayside detectors at the base of descending grades measure the heat a brake shoe puts into each wheel, replacing a manual air-brake test that requires stopping the train and walking it.▪ Canadian Pacific obtained a federal exemption in 2011 for its captive coal fleet and extended it in 2018 to grain, sulphur and potash, and air-brake failures are down 50% since 2019 (progressiverailroading.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. The exemption is Canadian, and after the KCS acquisition the majority of CPKC's route miles are in the U.S. and Mexico. Creel, 2026-09-17: "We're trying to bring that to the United States. We're working closely with the FRA… We're not there yet."

Train inspection portals are a purchasable product. CPKC operates four — two TIPS on the Canadian network, one of them on the Maple Creek, Saskatchewan subdivision with over 35 cameras producing 72 images per car and 100 GB of data per train, plus two RIPs at the Mexican borders (cpkcr.com factsheet, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Norfolk Southern operates 11 digital train inspection portals at 10 locations, imaging about 1,000 images per railcar (rtands.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web], and Duos Technologies, which supplies CPKC's Mexican units under a three-year subscription signed 2024-05-30, has 13 portals installed serving CN, CSX and others. On locomotive-mounted track inspection, CPKC's units analyse more than 600,000 miles on a 20,000-mile network, a figure whose period the October 2025 deck does not state; BNSF had 30 ODIN units in service at 2025-12-08 inspecting about 400,000 miles a year over 32,500 route miles, with 28 more units and a stated intention to reach about 5 million miles a year at full deployment in Q1 2026 (bnsf.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. At the December 2025 state of deployment CPKC covered more ground per route mile; at BNSF's stated full-deployment target BNSF covers roughly five times more ground per route mile [estimate: each company's stated mileage divided by its disclosed route miles; CPKC's 600,000 figure has no stated period].

Broken rail detection in dark territory is in-house engineering and is the smallest item in the portfolio: an antenna, solar panel and electronics box wired to the rail roughly every mile, at 10% of the cost of installing Centralized Traffic Control, deployed across more than 2,400 route miles of a 20,000-mile network. The hydrogen locomotive programme has two high-horsepower prototypes in mainline testing against a fleet of 2,307 units, and a joint venture with CSX, Hyion Technologies, was announced for low-horsepower units [deck: Q2 2026 earnings review, 2026-07-29, slide 22]. CPKC's 2026 guidance and its 2024–2028 targets are set without it. AI is at pilot and back-office scale: inspection-portal image analysis, expense-fraud detection, vendor-contract auditing and a customs documentation project, with no attributable cost or revenue figure published. Creel's own characterisation: "we're sticking our toe in the water… We're not going at warp speed."

Where technology shows in the numbers: FRA-reportable train accident frequency was 0.85 per million train-miles in FY2025 against CN's 1.84 and CSX's 3.08, and CPKC led all Class Is on that measure in 2023, 2024 and 2025.▪ Both FRA rates are annual-incentive-plan metrics with 30% of the short-term incentive weighted to safety. Both reversed in 2026: year-to-date train accident frequency was 0.93 against 0.68 and personal injury 0.94 against 0.85 [deck: Q2 2026 earnings review, slide 24], and Redd told the Q2 call "we are disappointed by these results."

The route products are the part no competitor can buy. Mexico Midwest Express, the Southeast Mexico Express with CSX, and the Canada–U.S.–Mexico land bridge are schedules and interchange rights built on track CPKC owns or operates. MMX moves San Luis Potosí to Chicago in 3.9 days against 4.0 by single-driver truck and 6.8 by the next-closest interchange rail option, a 43% transit advantage over the rail alternative▪ [deck: Investor Day 2023, slide 43], and it runs at roughly 70% capacity with a second train pair under evaluation. The upgraded SMX launched 2026-05-04 and grew volumes more than 30% between Q1 and Q2 2026 off a small base. Sections 3 and 4 cover them as competitive facts; among the technologies here they are the only ones that require owning the right-of-way.

3. Competitive advantages and moat assessment

Mexico produced 18% of FY2025 revenue and holds roughly 20% of net property, and CPKC publishes no profit, margin or return for it, so whether its largest block of capital earns above the cost of capital is unknown.

CPKC owns an asset nobody can rebuild and earns a return on it that is below its cost of capital. Both statements describe the same company in 2026.▪

The asset is roughly 20,000 route miles of continuous right-of-way and the only single-line freight rail route linking Canada, the United States and Mexico. It produced commercial results in FY2025: revenue grew 3.7% while the other five Class I networks grew between −3.1% and +1.5%, and freight revenue per carload rose 1% on a 3% carload increase against a fuel surcharge that declined C$168m. The advantage is real today and defensible for decades, because no one will lay a second parallel right-of-way and no new Class I has been built. Rivals began attacking it within weeks of the merger closing, and two of those attacks moved traffic. And the capital CPKC committed to acquire it has not earned its cost: FY2025 return on invested capital of 6.0% against a Surface Transportation Board determination of the railroad industry cost of capital at 10.68% for 2024 (stb.gov, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Excluding C$21,347m of KCS goodwill and acquired intangibles the figure is 8.8%, still below the hurdle and still last of six. Legacy CP earned about 15% in FY2019 and FY2020, two to four points above the five-peer mean. The US$31bn paid for Kansas City Southern moved CPKC from the top of that table to the bottom of it.

Management claims: Four, ranked by prominence. The network is unique and cannot be replicated: the 10-K opens on it and the Chief Marketing Officer told the Q2 2026 call "we've got a product that can't be replicated in the marketplace." The single-line route converts into revenue that did not exist before: land-bridge revenue from about C$100m in 2023 to over C$600m in 2026 with a path to C$1bn, and revenue synergies exiting 2026 at about C$1.5bn. Pricing runs above inflation: renewals "exceeding the top end of our long-term 3% to 4% outlook" on five consecutive calls. And returns and margins will reach the top of the industry: the 2024–2028 outlook, still on slide 22 of the September 2026 deck, targets high single-digit revenue growth, double-digit core adjusted EPS growth and a "return to double-digit Core adjusted ROIC".▪ One dated disclosure change belongs beside these. The FY2019 10-K named CN and BNSF as CP's primary rail competitors and described competition as varying by commodity, geography and mode; the FY2020 10-K replaced that with the generic paragraph still used in FY2025, naming only "other railways, motor carriers, ship and barge operators, and pipelines".

External sources: No sell-side research on CP exists in the local digest, so the external view is trade press and counterparty announcements. Coverage corroborates the corridor's commercial pull: CPKC won Schneider and Knight-Swift cross-border intermodal traffic from Union Pacific in 2023, and both became anchor customers on MMX (trains.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. The same article records the reverse flow: BNSF and J.B. Hunt moved their Mexico intermodal service to Ferromex via Eagle Pass effective 1 January 2024, on a routing they state is a day faster▪, with analyst Anthony B. Hatch quoted "This might be the first share shift away from CPKC." Union Pacific, CN and Grupo México announced Falcon Premium, a Canada–U.S.–Mexico interline intermodal service, on 26 April 2023, about a week after CPKC was formed (supplychaindive.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Union Pacific had already removed CP from the EMP domestic container pool in October 2022. The traffic moves both ways, which makes the corridor contested in both directions.

Ground-up view: The entry barrier is absolute and shared. A competing 20,000-mile right-of-way cannot be assembled, which excludes new entrants and does nothing about the five incumbents who already hold the same barrier and are the competition. Minimum efficient scale is reached with slack: 292 locomotives in storage at 2025-12-31, 82% freight-car in-service utilisation, FY2025 train miles up 1% on a 4% gross-ton-mile increase, and Q2 2026 average train speed up 7% with terminal dwell improving from 10.2 to 8.6 hours. Cost is not the binding constraint on the business; volume at origin is, and Q2 2026 coal revenue declined 18% on a 29% volume decline attributed to problems at the customer's mines and at the ports. Buyer power is diffuse in aggregate and concentrated by channel, as Section 1 sets out. Supplier power is rising on labour: about 75% of the workforce is unionised across 73 bargaining units and the current wage rate was set by a third-party arbitrator. Pricing regulation binds the largest line and registers maximum rates in Mexico with ATTRAPI, where the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolios can find no effective competition on particular movements, after which the regulator "could set rates for those movements or grant limited trackage rights to another railroad" (10-K FY2025, Item 1, Government Regulation — Mexico). A six-network oligopoly with an absolute entry barrier and slack capacity should produce returns above the cost of capital for the networks with the densest traffic and the fewest competing routings. UNP's 15.0% return and 59.8% operating ratio are what that looks like. CPKC's franchise is longer-haul and thinner, its largest line is rate-capped, its Mexican leg touches one border crossing against Union Pacific's six, and its capital base includes the price of buying the southern half.▪

Return on invested capital

ROIC = operating income × (1 − 25%) ÷ average invested capital, where invested capital is total debt including current maturities and finance leases, plus operating lease liabilities, plus total equity, less cash. A flat 25% rate is applied to all six companies so the comparison is not distorted by the FY2023 CPKC tax recovery or by jurisdictional rates. ROIC ex-goodwill uses the same numerator over the same base less goodwill and acquired intangibles.

The step between FY2020 and FY2021 is the November 2021 debt and share issue that funded the KCS purchase while KCS itself remained in a voting trust, so the 4.4% trough in FY2022 overstates the underlying deterioration. The pre-merger series held between 13.8% and 16.6% for eight years; the post-consolidation series has held between 5.4% and 6.0% for three and is rising about 0.3 points a year. On the 2024–2028 target of double-digit core adjusted ROIC: FY2025 core adjusted operating income of C$6,046m taxed at the disclosed 24.75% core adjusted rate gives C$4,550m over average invested capital of C$69,717m, or 6.5%, and 9.5% excluding goodwill and intangibles [estimate: core adjusted NOPAT reconstructed from disclosed revenue, the disclosed 59.9% core adjusted operating ratio and the disclosed tax rate; CPKC does not publish its ROIC definition, so the range across the two capital bases is 6.5% to 9.5%]. Reaching 10% on an unchanged base would require core adjusted operating income near C$9.3bn, about 50% above FY2025.

Return on incremental capital: Over FY2023 to FY2025 CPKC added C$916m of NOPAT on C$5,425m of additional invested capital, 16.9%, against BNSF at 16.8%, UNP at 27.1%, NSC at 44.5%, CN at −0.2% and CSX at −33.0%. That window is not clean in CPKC's favour: FY2023 holds only about 8.5 months of KCS operations against a year-end capital base that already held all of KCS, so a material part of the C$916m is the annualization of the acquisition and not a return on new capital. On the clean FY2024-to-FY2025 window invested capital declined from C$70,142m to C$69,291m, so no incremental return can be computed at all. Widened to FY2020–FY2025, which puts the acquisition capital in the denominator, the figure is 3.3%.

Versus peers: All six have a 31 December year end, so the latest-FY rows share an as-of date. Currency is stated per row and is not translated. Class I income statements present operating expenses as one undifferentiated block and none reports research and development, so operating margin is the first margin line available for all six.

CSX's Q2 2026 operating margin is 6.2 points above its FY2025 figure, so an argument built on CSX being the weakest operator in the group would already be wrong. CPKC's own 0.9-point decline is arithmetic: fuel surcharge revenue rose C$258m to C$608m while fuel expense rose C$213m, and removing both from the calculation gives an operating margin of 41.7% in Q2 2026 and 41.7% in Q2 2025.▪

Over time: Operating ratio, CPKC minus the mean of the five peers, where negative means CPKC is better: −2.5 points (FY2019), −6.2 (FY2020), +0.7 (FY2021), +0.4 (FY2022), −1.2 (FY2023), +0.1 (FY2024), −1.1 (FY2025).▪ Return on invested capital, CPKC minus the five-peer mean: +2.1 points (FY2019), +4.2 (FY2020), −6.0 (FY2023), −5.8 (FY2024), −5.2 (FY2025). The margin advantage disappeared at consolidation and has oscillated around zero for four years without a trend. The returns gap is closing at about 0.4 points a year, which at that pace takes a decade to undo.

Pricing test in detail: FY2025 freight revenue per carload rose 1% and per ton-mile was flat. Stripping fuel surcharge from both years gives 6.058 cents against 5.945, +1.9%; removing the disclosed C$154m of favourable FX as well leaves +0.7%. In H1 2026 the same construction gives −0.5% per ton-mile and +3.2% per carload. Contracted wage inflation is 3% a year to the end of 2027, and compensation and benefits per average employee rose 1.5% in FY2025. So the pricing claim holds on the measure management prices to and fails on the measure that scales with the work performed, and the difference is that CPKC is hauling roughly the same number of boxes further at a lower rate per ton-mile.▪ By line in FY2025, against a common C$168m surcharge headwind: coal +5% per ton-mile, grain +1%, potash −3%, intermodal −3%, automotive −7%. The two lines where the single-line Canada–U.S.–Mexico route is the selling point posted the weakest per-ton-mile yield of the five; coal, a bulk haul with no differentiation argument attached, posted the strongest.

Where this places the advantage: CPKC belongs in the middle band: an advantage that earns a return on the operating assets today and is defensible for a long time, but is open to erosion as rivals route around it, and one whose acquisition price has not been earned back.▪ Three facts keep it below the top tier. Rivals attacked the corridor within weeks and two attacks moved accounts. The two lines that depend on the differentiator price worst. And the return on the capital committed is below the industry cost of capital and below all five comparable networks.

Business-model analogues: Canadian National is the closest listed comparison: same country, same regulator, same maximum revenue entitlement on grain, same one-segment rail economics, and 11.6% ROIC on a capital base with no acquisition premium in it. The analogue breaks where CPKC's franchise does not overlap, because CN has no Mexican concession and no single-line southern route. Union Pacific is the same asset class run at higher density with six Mexican gateways, 15.0% ROIC and a 59.8% operating ratio, and it is the benchmark the "best margins in the industry" claim has to clear; it breaks as an analogue because UNP never paid a control premium of this size. The sharpest structural analogue is BNSF: an irreplaceable network bought at a large premium in 2010, whose balance sheet still holds US$15,351m of goodwill from that purchase, which earned 8.2% ROIC in FY2025 and 10.4% excluding the goodwill.▪ CPKC has the same shape one merger cycle later, and sixteen years of operating improvement have not lifted BNSF's return on its acquisition-inflated capital base above 9.7% in any year since 2019. BNSF is not itself a listed equity; it files on registered debt and Berkshire Hathaway is the public security.

4. Competitive landscape and market sizing

CPKC is the smallest of the six North American Class I railroads: sixth of six on revenue at US$10,770m equivalent, 11.1% of the six-carrier total; third on revenue ton-miles among the five that disclose them; and last on revenue per route mile.▪ It leads in three places: Canadian export potash, where it moves the large majority of Canpotex volume to Vancouver and, jointly with Union Pacific, all of it to Portland; Mexican automotive, where it reaches 90% of Mexican assembly plants▪ [deck: investor presentation September 2026, slide 30]; and the Canada–U.S.–Mexico single-line land bridge, which no other carrier offers at all.

Conversion at the C$1.40 average rate CPKC discloses for 2025. The Herfindahl-Hirschman index on these shares is 1,863. A Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern combination takes the merged share to 37.7% and the index to 2,493, a rise of 630; a BNSF–CSX response would take it to 3,190.▪ Creel put the same arithmetic institutionally: "we've got no place for an industry that 3 decades ago was 30 railroads. Now we're living in a world there's 6. And if this gets approved, it's a path to 2."

The national index understates competition in one direction and overstates it in the other, because railroads compete corridor by corridor and most origin-destination pairs are served by one or two carriers. East of the Mississippi the structure is a CSX/NS duopoly, west of it UP/BNSF, in Canada CN/CPKC, and in Mexico CPKC against Grupo México's Ferromex and Ferrosur. CPKC is present in three of those four theatres.▪

Three mechanisms cap CPKC's pricing and only one is a competitor: the Canada Transportation Act maximum revenue entitlement on about 7% of revenue; the Mexican concession, with maximum rates registered with ATTRAPI and a 1.25%-of-gross-revenue duty; and competing modes everywhere else, where the binding competitor differs by line — pipelines in energy and chemicals, trucks in intermodal and automotive, CN in Canadian bulk, and ocean-carrier routing in international intermodal.

Revenue per ton-mile differs across the six. CPKC earns 4.81 U.S. cents per revenue ton-mile, the lowest of the five carriers that disclose ton-miles, against CN 5.00, UNP 5.44, CSX 6.49 and NSC 6.62. That is mix and geography: CPKC's book is 36% bulk with long hauls and a statutory cap on the largest bulk line, against eastern merchandise books at CSX and NSC.▪

Market sizing

The directly contested pool is US$97,333m of FY2025 Class I revenue, built above from each carrier's own income statement. The four U.S.-domiciled Class Is earned US$74,200m; adding CPKC's U.S.-earned revenue of C$5,124m (US$3,660m) and CN's unbroken-out U.S. revenue puts the U.S. Class I total above US$78bn, and at the AAR's stated 94% Class I share of U.S. rail revenue that implies roughly US$83bn of total U.S. rail freight revenue [estimate: 78/0.94] (aar.org, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Against that, U.S. trucking revenue was US$906bn in 2024 and 76.9% of the freight bill, implying a US$1,178bn total U.S. freight market (trucking.org, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Rail earns roughly 7% of the freight bill while moving about 40% of long-distance ton-miles, so truck-to-rail conversion reduces the shipper's spend.

MMX runs at roughly 70% capacity. The Canada–Mexico land bridge went from about C$100m in 2023 to about C$600m expected in 2026 with a stated path to C$1bn. Total merger revenue synergies exit 2026 at C$1.4–1.5bn. Against FY2025 revenue of C$15,078m, the land-bridge franchise no competitor can offer single-line is about 4% of revenue today and 7% at the C$1bn target. The deck publishes no addressable-market figure, so there is no management total to check.

The structural event: UP–NS

Union Pacific agreed to acquire Norfolk Southern on 2025-07-28 and both shareholder bases approved on 2025-11-14. The STB rejected the first joint application as incomplete on 2026-01-16, accepted a revised application effective 2026-05-28, held the proceeding in abeyance pending supplemental information, then lifted the abeyance on 2026-08-18 and set a schedule: notices of intent to participate due 2026-09-04; comments, protests, requests for conditions and responsive or inconsistent applications due 2026-11-18; replies and rebuttal 2027-02-16; final briefs 2027-05-28; a public hearing in spring 2027 on a date to be set in a later decision; and a statutory decision deadline of 2027-08-28 (stb.gov PR-26-21, accessed 2026-09-21; thompsonhine.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Union Pacific expects completion in 2027 (UNP 10-Q 2026-Q2, Note 18). CPKC spent C$27m in H1 2026 on analysis and advocacy in the proceeding, C$14m of it in Q2, excluded from core adjusted results as a new significant item with no FY2025 equivalent.

What CPKC will ask for, reported ahead of its 2026-11-18 filing (freightwaves.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]: trackage rights over NS's former Wabash main line from Mexico, Missouri to St. Louis with Terminal Railroad Association close-the-gap rights; removal of commodity restrictions on its existing Beaumont–Rosenberg and Victoria–Robstown rights over UP; new Louisiana rights at Baton Rouge and on the Shreveport–Houston Lufkin subdivision; strengthened Detroit–Chicago rights over NS with expanded interchanges; a Knoche Yard–Kansas City Terminal connection and a Polo Line paired-track arrangement; service-level guarantees; and an STB prohibition on NS or UP acquiring CPKC's Wylie, Texas automotive and intermodal terminal. CSX is asking for the same Kansas City–St. Louis corridor plus a 50% divestiture of UP's line and dispatching control of Neff Yard, and BNSF for 824 miles of overhead rights over NS to Bethlehem, Pennsylvania and a neutral switching railroad covering roughly 900 UP-served Houston petrochemical customers. Creel describes CPKC and CSX as having "never been closer" while the two file competing requests for the same trackage.

One competitive change is already in force and does not depend on approval. Under an agreement of July 2026, Union Pacific receives expanded operating rights over CN's former Elgin, Joliet & Eastern corridor around Chicago and CN gains operating rights over Union Pacific's network between Memphis and the Eagle Pass gateway to Ferromex▪ (railway-news.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. A second, separate settlement agreement, under which CN will not oppose the merger, is contingent on STB approval and closing, and would give CN NS's Kansas City Terminal and Terminal Railroad Association interests, Tuscola–East St. Louis overhead rights, St. Louis–Kansas City customer rights and Neff Yard access (cn.ca, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. CPKC's answer is route geometry: a three-carrier interline cannot match a single-line move, and western Canadian origins, which supply the majority of the land-bridge traffic, would route east through Chicago before turning south. That answer is sound on miles and untested on price.

Splitting CPKC's own density by country using the geographic revenue note and Item 2 mileage gives Canada US$616k per route mile, Mexico US$625k and the United States US$416k [estimate: FY2025 geographic revenue divided by Item 2 country mileage at C$1.40; interline revenue allocation across borders is not disclosed, and the measure sets an allocation inside an integrated three-country network against standalone railroad totals]. On that basis the U.S. portion of CPKC's network earns about 59% of what CSX earns per route mile and 65% of NSC's, and the shortfall concentrates in the legacy Soo Line, DM&E and KCS U.S. lines.

Grain, potash and fertilizers: CPKC reports three lines where CN reports one group, so the basket is the like-for-like comparison. CPKC's grain-plus-potash-plus-fertilizer revenue of C$4,280m exceeds CN's C$3,658m, and its 85,953m ton-miles exceed CN's 67,773m. Applying CN's own disclosed sub-split, CPKC's grain line alone is about 10% above CN's grain-only revenue and its potash-plus-fertilizer lines about 45% above CN's fertilizer revenue [estimate: CN's commodity-group percentage table applied to C$3,658m]. Physical share runs the other way. In crop year 2024-25 CN moved approximately 31 million tonnes of western Canadian grain, about 1 million above its previous record, while CPKC moved "in excess of 27 million tonnes", its highest since 2020-21 — roughly 53/47 in CN's favour▪ (world-grain.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. A longer Grain Monitoring Program share series would settle whether that gap has been widening. CPKC's revenue lead on a smaller tonnage share comes from the U.S. grain franchise and the Mexican destinations the merger created, neither of which the entitlement covers.

Intermodal: CPKC's 1,780.6k units are 44% of Norfolk Southern's and 59% of CSX's, and it grew fastest of the group in FY2025 at +8.4%. Revenue per unit of C$1,505 is below CN's C$1,742 on the same currency and basis, and well above CSX's US$692 and NSC's US$742, which reflects long hauls and a 54% domestic mix in 53-foot boxes against short port-drayage moves. The international half depends on routing CPKC does not control: the Gemini Cooperation between Hapag-Lloyd and Maersk, which began February 2025, was named as the FY2025 growth driver at Vancouver and Saint John, and in Q2 2026 those same ports were named as declines. CN holds exclusive rail access to Prince Rupert, whose Fairview container terminal rose 20% to 885,797 TEU in 2025 (rupertport.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web], and to Halifax; CPKC reaches Saint John by haulage agreement and owns Lázaro Cárdenas. In Q2 2026 CPKC's intermodal units declined 1% while CSX's rose 9%, NSC's 5% and UNP's 4%.

Automotive: CPKC earns US$3,916 per automotive carload, 26% above the next-highest disclosed figure (NSC at US$3,121) and 28% above CN, because its ton-miles per carload are about 23,000 against CN's 15,300: finished vehicles moving from Mexican plants to Canada in a closed loop.▪ Q2 2026 was a record automotive quarter at +19% revenue on +8% volume on the FX-adjusted basis management presents.

Coal and forest products are where CPKC is most exposed and furthest behind. Coal is its second-lowest-yielding line at 4.31 cents per ton-mile, and almost all Canadian metallurgical tonnage originates at Elk Valley Resources, owned by Glencore 77%, Nippon Steel 20% and POSCO 3% since 2024-07-11; Glencore files no SEC reports, so mine-side production data is not obtainable from filings. CPKC's forest products revenue of C$792m is 43% of CN's C$1,839m on 43% of the ton-miles, and it was the one CPKC line whose FY2025 revenue declined.

Metals, minerals and consumer products is the line where CPKC gained on CN in both FY2025 and H1 2026: C$1,792m of revenue at 9.33 cents per ton-mile against CN's C$1,962m at 7.25 cents, and 66% more revenue per carload, because CN's group is diluted by iron ore moving in heavy low-rate unit trains.

Share counter-evidence, ranked by how much it changes the structure

  • UP–NS approval converts six carriers into five and sets up a BNSF–CSX response. The index rises 630 on approval and 1,327 if a second combination follows; CPKC would go from sixth of six to smallest of four, facing two transcontinental systems. Decision due by 2027-08-28.
  • CN's Memphis–Eagle Pass haulage rights over UP are in force and not merger-contingent. CN can offer a routed Canada-to-Mexico product now.
  • BNSF and J.B. Hunt moved Mexico cross-border intermodal from CPKC's Laredo routing to Ferromex via Eagle Pass, on a routing they state is a day faster. This is a lost account on the flagship cross-border franchise, and neither carrier has published its size.
  • CN moved more western Canadian grain than CPKC in crop year 2024-25, on the largest line CPKC has and the one under a statutory revenue cap.
  • Coal origin concentration. Q2 2026 ton-miles −29% on Elk Valley mine and port problems, against CN −5.3% on the same basin in H1 2026. CPKC's exposure to a single origin is a structural feature of the franchise.
  • Prince Rupert grew 20% in 2025 and CPKC cannot reach it. CN's exclusive access to Prince Rupert and Halifax excludes CPKC from two Canadian container gateways.
  • Pipelines set the ceiling in energy and chemicals. CPKC's own description of DRUbit as cost competitive with pipeline transportation concedes the point.
  • Autonomous trucking. Creel's position is "it's not if, it's when", with border crossings as the barrier that delays the effect on CPKC. Aurora Innovation had accumulated 5.3 million commercial miles through 2026-04-30 and holds ten approved driverless routes including Dallas–Laredo (sec.gov, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Cross-border is 41% of FY2025 freight revenue, so the border friction that makes MMX work is also the protection; it is no protection on intra-U.S. legs.

5. Value chain and profit pools

Five inputs account for almost all of CPKC's cost base, and the railway layer earns the highest margin disclosed anywhere in the chain.

CPKC's 37.2% operating margin is the highest disclosed margin at any layer of this chain, above Wabtec's Freight operating margin of 19.5% and Mosaic's Potash gross margin of 32.7%.▪ Inside CPKC, each dollar of FY2025 revenue divides into 17.1 cents of compensation, 15.0 of purchased services, 13.4 of depreciation, 11.5 of fuel, 3.1 of materials, 2.7 of equipment rents and 37.2 of operating income; capital spending of 20.6 cents per revenue dollar is additional.

What the haul costs the shipper, against what the shipper sells: Tonnes per car are not disclosed, so each per-tonne figure below is derived from CPKC's own carload and ton-mile data over an assumed average haul distance, and each percentage is a range.

Commodity CPKC revenue per unit Derived freight per tonne or unit Reference value of the goods Freight as % of value
Potash, FY2025 C$3,618/carload ~C$36/t ≈ US$26/t Mosaic MOP US$255/t fob mine ~10%

Where the haul is a large fraction of what the shipper sells — grain at roughly 7% of canola and more of wheat — Parliament capped the price by formula. Where the haul is under 1% of what the shipper sells, automotive earned 26.43 cents per ton-mile in Q2 2026, 5.5x the coal yield of 4.82 cents in the same quarter, and no regulator intervenes.▪

The binding constraint is at the origin. Every disclosed capacity measure shows slack and it widened through Q2 2026: 292 locomotives in storage, 12.7% of the fleet; 82% freight-car in-service utilisation; FY2025 gross ton-miles up 4% on train miles up 1%.▪ Creel on the Q2 2026 call: "We're in a very good position relative to locomotives, relative to car capacity, relative to track capacity. The only thing we need to flex up on when the business and the growth comes is add incremental headcount." Q2 2026 measured where the constraint binds. CPKC's coal revenue declined 18% and its ton-miles 29%, which the 10-Q attributes to lower production and maintenance at the mines and the ports. Glencore's own half-year report puts the same event on the mine side: group steelmaking coal production of 13.5 Mt in H1 2026 was 2.2 Mt (14%) below H1 2025 on lower Elk Valley throughput, yields, pit sequencing and weather, Canadian production declined 19% to 10.3 Mt, and full-year guidance was cut from 30–34 Mt to 30–32 Mt (glencore.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. Two filings on opposite sides of the interface describe the same shortfall and neither mentions rail capacity.

Lead times and who is locked up: Wabtec's Freight backlog of about US$22.5bn is 2.8 years of FY2025 Freight sales, so locomotive slots are booked years ahead. CPKC's own commitments run to 2033: Note 26 records C$4,397m at 2025-12-31 for the Celaya–NBA Line Railway Bypass, the Mexican concession, other capital expenditure, bulk fuel, locomotive maintenance and other goods and services, 29% of FY2025 revenue committed forward. Customers commit nothing comparable, because contract liabilities are immaterial.

Customer-side economics: Nutrien's controllable cash cost of potash was US$58 per tonne in 2025 and Mosaic's MOP price US$255 per tonne fob mine, against a CPKC haul of roughly US$26 per tonne — about 45% of the producer's own cash cost of making the product and about 10% of the fob-mine price. The freight is affordable even at Mosaic's weakest recent potash margin; the exposure runs the other way, because CPKC's volumes follow Canpotex's offshore sales programme. In the container chain the rail rate did not move with the ocean rate: CPKC's intermodal revenue per carload rose 12% year over year in Q2 2026, which the 10-Q attributes to higher fuel surcharge revenue and higher freight rates without splitting them, while the ocean leg rose about 2.5x from January to September 2026. And the truck substitute sets the ceiling on the merchandise and domestic intermodal book — CPKC's CMO attributed the 2026 conversion opportunity to conditions outside CPKC's control: "higher fuel prices, tighter regulatory enforcement and reduced trucking capacity" (Q1 2026 call).

Bargaining power is moving in CPKC's favour at one interface and against it at another. Against Wabtec, CPKC insourced a subset of locomotive maintenance from Q4 2024, which raised materials expense 17% to C$474m while purchased services declined 4%, and it added Progress Rail as a second OEM with deliveries from H2 2026 — this against a supplier whose own 10-K describes an installed base of nearly 24,600 locomotives and 58% of Freight segment sales coming from aftermarket. Against labour, the wage rate is set by an arbitrator for two more years. Against the diesel index, neither CPKC nor its shippers set the price: the surcharge covered 86% of fuel expense in FY2025 when prices declined and 98% in Q2 2026 when On-Highway Diesel rose 52%, which is the opposite of what a simple lag would produce.▪

Circular financing: Note 4 records no material contract liabilities at either year end, so there is no customer prepayment. Guarantees total C$16m. One equity stake was sold to a customer's parent: CPKC sold its 50% Panama Canal Railway interest to APM Terminals Panama Rail LP, a subsidiary of A.P. Moller-Maersk, on 2025-04-01 for US$350m gross and a pre-tax gain of US$232m (C$333m), while Maersk is simultaneously a Gemini alliance member routing containers onto CPKC and CPKC's partner in a 2021 Vancouver transload facility. The Mexican concession duty is a royalty on the whole Mexican book at 1.25% of gross revenues, roughly C$34m a year [estimate: 1.25% of C$2,711m of Mexican geographic revenue; the duty is levied on CPKCM gross revenues, which may differ from the geographic disclosure].

6. Secular and industry trends

CPKC's freight demand is set at the origin. The nine lines divide into four mechanisms, and the two largest groups are supply-constrained.▪

Energy and industrial merchandise (ECP, metals, forest) 5,482 36.4 Alberta refining and petrochemical runs, U.S. Gulf refinery demand, U.S. housing starts, steel trade flows
Coal 1,025 6.8 Elk Valley Resources output; Powder River Basin interchange receipts

Non-freight 302 2.0 Leases, switching, passenger contracts, fibre-optic and subsurface rights

In Q2 2026 CPKC's coal ton-miles declined 29% while Glencore's realised steelmaking coal price rose to US$206.90 per tonne from US$167.10 a year earlier. Price rose and volume collapsed, which places the cause on the mine side and not on demand.

Growth attribution: what the realized numbers contain

Against the plan: At the June 2023 Investor Day CPKC set high single-digit revenue growth for 2024–2028, double-digit core adjusted EPS growth with "line of sight to… meaningfully double our EPS over that time frame", 3–4% pricing and revenue synergies of C$1.5bn-plus by year five.▪ FY2025 revenue grew 3.7% headline and 5.4% excluding fuel surcharge, on ton-mile growth of 3.8%. H1 2026 grew 5.0% headline and 2.4% excluding surcharge, on ton-mile growth of 2.8%. Removing the disclosed fuel-price and FX effects from both sides, underlying revenue growth was +4.2% in FY2025 against +3.8% of ton-miles, and +2.9% in H1 2026 against +2.8% of ton-miles. Real yield growth was about half a point in FY2025 and approximately zero in the half. Two years into a five-year plan, growth is running at roughly half the target rate, and the gap is not a pricing failure in the renewal book: it is that the base business did not grow and mix diluted realized yield.▪

Against the ultimate driver: volume is set by the crop, the mine and the ocean alliance. Weighted by line, FY2025's 7,962m of additional ton-miles priced at 6.19 cents against a system average of 6.73, 8% below, because the lines that grew — grain at 5.24 cents, intermodal at 6.96, potash at 3.32, coal at 4.31 — are at or below the system average while the line that shrank most, energy and chemicals at 7.70 cents, is above it. In H1 2026 the mix ran the other way for an unhelpful reason: incremental ton-miles priced at 7.12 cents against a 6.87-cent average because the largest decline was coal, so the collapse of the lowest-yield line is yield-accretive on the reported statistics while removing volume.

Grain alone added 4,687m ton-miles at 5.19 cents, worth about C$243m of freight revenue against total underlying revenue growth of C$214m in the half. The record Canadian harvest accounts for more than all of the underlying revenue growth in the period.▪

Against industry dollars and units: CPKC's carload count includes intermodal units and is comparable with the AAR measure. CPKC's carloads-plus-intermodal declined 0.8% in H1 2026 while North American Class I volume for the first 36 weeks of 2026 rose 3.0%, U.S. railroads 3.4%, Canadian railroads 1.4% and Mexican railroads 7.1% (railpace.com, accessed 2026-09-21) [web]. The periods do not match — CPKC's is a reported half-year, the AAR figure runs to mid-September — and the AAR aggregate includes CPKC, so the ex-CPKC industry rate is slightly higher than shown. On units, CPKC lost share in the half against every geographic aggregate including the Canadian one.
